challenges.description: Pseudo-labels from VLM auto-labelling may contain noisy labels in edge cases, and retraining on wrong labels can cause confirmation bias and performance degradation.

challenges.description: Simple condition-based automation scripts stop the whole pipeline or require manual engineer intervention when boundary cases occur.

responses.description: Using Monte Carlo Dropout to decompose uncertainty and select ambiguous data for the learning cycle.

title: From Labeling to Deployment: VLM and Agentic AI-Based Autonomous Vision Inspection - LG AI Research BLOG
summary: LG AI Research describes an autonomous vision inspection framework that uses Monte Carlo Dropout to isolate uncertain samples, a Vision-Language Model to auto-label them through a three-stage training pipeline, and embedding-space similarity checks to filter noisy labels before retraining. The page reports a 93.13% accuracy versus 88.29% for random sampling.
evidence: Applying this precise uncertainty sampling mechanism yielded an accuracy of 93.13%, representing a significant +4.84%p improvement compared to random sampling (88.29%) under identical data computational conditions.

fields.autonomy_cues: The uncertainty samples precisely selected in the previous stage bypass human operators and automatically receive ground truth labels via a Vision-Language Model (VLM).

challenges.description: Incorrectly assigned pseudo-labels from auto-labeling can be fed into retraining, causing the model to reinforce its own errors.
challenges.quote: Feeding incorrectly assigned labels directly into retraining can cause the model to fall into confirmation bias—reinforcing its own errors—and lead to severe performance degradation[13].

challenges.description: Subtle label noise may be introduced into pseudo-labels under extreme edge cases or optical limitation conditions.
challenges.quote: there remains a possibility that subtle label noise (noisy labels) may be introduced into pseudo-labels under extreme edge cases or optical limitation conditions.

responses.description: A noise-robust learning policy based on similarity analysis in the visual feature embedding space flags samples whose labels conflict with neighbouring visually identical samples.
responses.quote: To prevent this, the proposed framework adopts a noise-robust learning policy based on similarity analysis within the visual feature embedding space.

responses.description: A multi-stage VLM training pipeline with domain fine-tuning and reasoning reinforcement learning using a tailored reward model improves labeling consistency and reliability.

title: Building agents that transact with Anchor Browser and AgentCore payments
summary: The page describes how Anchor Browser integrates with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore payments so that AI agents can autonomously pay for x402-protected web resources and APIs within a configured budget. It also explains the challenges of building payment handling, key management and spend controls into agents without a managed service.

fields.human_oversight: AgentCore payments enforces configurable spending limits at the infrastructure layer and provides observability into payment attempts, approvals, denials and settlements through Amazon CloudWatch.

challenges.description: Without a managed payment service, agents stall on HTTP 402 responses and developers must build the full payment stack, which is complex to build and maintain.
challenges.quote: Today, developers must build the entire payment stack. This effort spans four categories of complexity:

challenges.description: Without hard spending limits enforced at infrastructure level, bugs, retry loops or prompt injection can trigger unintended payments.
challenges.quote: Without hard spending limits enforced at the infrastructure level, a bug, retry loop, prompt injection, or inadvertent access can trigger unintended payments.

challenges.description: Private keys inside the agent runtime share an execution environment with untrusted web pages and third-party tools, risking disclosure of credentials controlling funds.
challenges.quote: When private keys reside inside the agent runtime, they share an execution environment with untrusted web pages, third-party tools, and external dependencies.

challenges.description: Signing infrastructure accessible from the runtime could let a threat actor access the key or redirect payments to an address under unauthorised control.
challenges.quote: If the signing infrastructure is accessible from the runtime, a threat actor can attempt to access the key or redirect payments to an address under unauthorized control.

challenges.description: Payment must occur within the same browser session, otherwise session recordings and live view no longer match what actually executed, which affects traceability.
challenges.quote: Otherwise, session recordings and live view no longer match what actually executed.

challenges.description: Agents retrying a paid endpoint in a loop continue to authorise payments until manual intervention occurs.
challenges.quote: An agent retrying a paid endpoint in a loop continues to authorize payments until manual intervention occurs.

responses.description: Payment keys are kept out of the agent runtime so the signing flow is not exposed to untrusted inputs.
responses.quote: Effective mitigation requires that the key doesn’t enter the runtime in the first place.

responses.description: Spending limits are enforced at the infrastructure layer, with configurable per-session and per-transaction budgets.
responses.quote: AgentCore payments manages wallet connectivity, enforces configurable spending limits at the infrastructure layer, and processes payments through the x402 protocol.

responses.description: Payment attempts, approvals, denials and settlements are logged to Amazon CloudWatch for observability and audit.
responses.quote: It also provides observability into payment attempts, approvals, denials, and settlements through Amazon CloudWatch.
